source.citation: Georget, F., Lothenbach, B., Wilson, W., Zunino, F., Scrivener, K. L. (2022). Stability of hemicarbonate under cement paste-like conditions. Cement and Concrete Research 153, 106692.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF, open access CC BY-NC-ND 4.0): Tables 3 to 9 read in the text layer and checked on the rendered pages; the sample preparation from Section 2
transcription.note: All samples are synthetic C3A-based slurries cured 28 days at 20 C; nothing in the paper varies time or temperature, and there is no carbonation by CO2: the 'carbonate series' replaces portlandite by calcite in the starting mix (zeta_CO3 = n_CaCO3/(n_CaCO3 + n_Ca(OH)2), Fig. 4 axis), which is equivalent to a CO2 uptake at fixed Ca/Al. The superscript N of the tables marks the nominal composition. The authors' model curves (Figs. 4a, 7a, 11a) are raster images and are not digitized: their numbers are in the authors' dataset, transcribed in Georget2021data.json. Table 1 (reference crystal structures) and Table 2 (basal spacings) are not transcribed.

c3a_per_sample.description: Synthesized cubic C3A per sample; the other reactants are added in the stoichiometric molar ratios of the target AFm phase.

c3a_purity.description: C3A content of the synthesized powder, percent, by XRD-Rietveld assuming no amorphous content; the remaining 3 % is free lime.

free_lime_in_c3a.description: Free lime in the synthesized C3A powder, percent.

extra_portlandite.description: Portlandite added beyond stoichiometry to every sample ('0.5 g for 10 g of C3A'), to keep portlandite present.

rutile.description: Rutile added as XRD internal standard, 'around 2.5 wt%'.

water_solid_mixing.description: Water/solid mass ratio at mixing (boiled deionized water, 1600 rpm for 2 min).

extra_water.description: Boiled deionized water added after 1 hour in the glove box.

water_solid_total.description: Total water/solid ratio after the extra water, printed 'around 2.7'.

curing_time.description: Curing time, sealed PE pots under N2 at about 99 % relative humidity.

cacl2_excess.description: Excess CaCl2 added to the chloride samples to compensate the chloride left in solution, as predicted by preliminary GEMS modeling.

na_in_calcium_carbonate.description: Upper bound of the Na impurity of the calcium carbonate used, percent ('Na content up to 0.2%'); alkalis were not measured in solution.

model_pH_carbonate_series.description: pH the default Cemdata18 calculation gives along the carbonate series, set by the alkalis of the raw materials.

model_Ca_carbonate_series.description: Total Ca the default Cemdata18 calculation gives, set by portlandite, printed '16.3 mmol/kg'.

model_zeta_katoite_limit.description: Below this zeta_CO3 the default Cemdata18 calculation gives katoite, portlandite and hemicarbonate.

model_zeta_hc_dominant_low.description: Lower end of the zeta_CO3 range (0.2 to 0.65) where hemicarbonate is the dominant phase in the default calculation.

model_zeta_hc_dominant_high.description: Upper end of that range; above it monocarbonate replaces hemicarbonate.

edx_S_Ca_hc_3pct_gypsum.description: S/Ca of the hemicarbonate at 3 % gypsum, 'approximately equal to 0.025', about 10 % of the interlayer positions taken by sulfate.

edx_S_Ca_ms_10pct_gypsum.description: S/Ca of the high-S cluster at 10 % gypsum, attributed to monosulfate ('around 0.175').

edx_S_Ca_hc_10pct_gypsum.description: S/Ca of the low-S cluster at 10 % gypsum, attributed to hemicarbonate ('~0.075', about 33 % of the carbonate positions), which the authors take as the maximum substitution.

carbonate_series.location: Table 7, p. 8: supernatant after 28 days at 20 C, pH by electrode, Ca by ICP-OES; phases by XRD (wet and dried) and Raman. Hc hemicarbonate, Mc monocarbonate, CH portlandite, CC calcite. Two samples at 0.5

sulfate_series.location: Table 8, p. 10: gypsum added (percent) to the hemicarbonate mix (zeta_CO3 = 0.5); SO4 by ion chromatography, printed N/A (null) without gypsum; Ms monosulfate. No ettringite was found by XRD in any sample

chloride_series.location: Table 9, p. 12: carbonate of the hemicarbonate replaced by chloride (chi_2Cl = 1 is Friedel's salt); Cl by ion chromatography, printed N/A (null) at 0; Fssol the Friedel's salt-hemicarbonate solid solution, Fs Friedel's salt

c3a_hydration_degree.location: Section 6.2, p. 14: degree of C3A hydration estimated by comparing Table 9 with the authors' solid-solution model

afm_thermodynamic_data.location: Table 3, p. 4: AFm phases at 25 C and 1 atm; the number in parentheses is the hydration state (water molecules); most_common_state is the table's bold; references are the paper's reference numbers ([36] is Cemdata18)

afm_solubility_products.location: Table 4, p. 5: log Ks0 at 25 C and 1 atm, calculated from Table 3, for dissolution into Ca+2, AlO2-, HO- (OH-), the interlayer anion (SO4-2, CO3-2, Cl-, HSiO3- for stratlingite) and water, the CEMDATA18/GEMS primary species

hemicarbonate_sulfate_solid_solution.location: Table 5, p. 5: the CO3-SO4-OH hemicarbonate sublattice solid solution of Section 7.1 (the caption, a misprint, names it the Cl-CO3-AFm model); ideal mixing (Section 7.1). The water site is printed e.g. '{H2O}5.50.5', read as 5.5 water and 0.5 vacancy on a site of 6 (the sum is 6 in every row of Tables 5 and 6)

chloride_carbonate_solid_solution.location: Table 6, p. 5: the Cl-CO3-OH AFm regular sublattice solid solution of Section 7.2, fitted by hand on Hobbs (2001)

notes: Default model (Section 2.8): GEMS 3.7 with TSolMod, the PSI/Nagra database and Cemdata18; in Cemdata18 the hemicarbonate, monocarbonate and Friedel's salt are separate pure phases, with the OH/SO4-AFm solid solution only. That is the model ChemistryLab's Cemdata18 reproduces.

Measured against default model (carbonate series, Fig. 4b and Table 7): katoite at 0.25 and its absence above, hemicarbonate at 0.25 to 0.75, monocarbonate from 0.5, all as predicted; calcite at 0.75 is not predicted (the figure marks it red), which the authors put down to unreacted C3A or to carbonation during preparation or drying.

Measured against default model (sulfate series, Section 5): the default Cemdata18 predicts ettringite with monocarbonate; no ettringite was found, but sulfate in hemicarbonate at 3 % gypsum and monosulfate at 10 %.

Table 4 misprints, transcribed values unaffected: the Friedel's salt equation is printed with (HO)2 in place of Cl2, and the two monocarbonate equations release 0.5 CO3-2 where the formula has one CO3.

Tables 5 and 6 appear to swap two Gibbs energies. The monocarbonate of Table 6, with log Ks0 = -31.27 (0.2 above the -31.47 of Table 4), should have dfG = -7337.46 + 0.2 x 5.708 = -7336.32 kJ/mol, the value Table 5 prints for hemicarbonate; and the hemicarbonate of Table 5, whose log Ks0 (-29.13) is unchanged from Table 4, should keep the -7335.97 kJ/mol of Table 3, the value Table 6 prints for monocarbonate. The monocarbonate of Table 5 (-30.47, one unit above Table 4) checks: -7337.46 + 5.708 = -7331.75. Both values are transcribed as printed.

The proof-of-concept solid solutions (Tables 5 and 6) are presented by the authors as tentative ('should only be used with caution'); Table 5 lowers the monocarbonate stability by one log unit following Nedyalkova et al. (2020).

The authors' dataset (ref. [41], Zenodo, doi 10.5281/zenodo.5115540, CC BY 4.0) holds the raw XRD, TGA, Raman, SEM-EDX data, the GEMS project and the calculated phase assemblages; its model curves and the recipes its scripts state are in Georget2021data.json.
